newsitem.title: USA: AT&T, Hewlett in electronic commerce pact.
newsitem.headline: AT&T, Hewlett in electronic commerce pact.

text.p: AT&T Corp. and Hewlett-Packard Co. said Monday they agreed to a multi-phase alliance designed to make it easier for companies to conduct business on the Internet and intranets.

In a joint statement, the companies said they will integrate their technologies to create electronic storefront systems that will allow merchants to host Web sites capable of secure electronic transactions. Such electronic commerce systems will be built around AT&T's SecureBuy Service, which provides infrastructure and management.
The partners said they would collaborate with iCat Corp. and other electronic commerce software developers to help merchants process orders and serve customers.
The alliance will also build on AT&T's existing relationship with Open Market Inc. in which AT&T has integrated Open Market's electronic commerce software into its SecureBuy system.
AT&T and H-P said they will bring together their current electronic commerce, network services, hardware, software, consulting and support to deliver additional new products and services.
AT&T Labs and H-P Labs will collaborate to develop new technologies to improve the reliability and continuous availability of Internet-based network services.

AT&T, based in Basking Ridge, N.J., said it plans to recruit H-P's nearly 15,000 resellers to join its Marketing Alliance Programme as agents to sell AT&T's Web site services. The services include Web hosting, which provides companies with Web sites situated on AT&T computers.

It was not evident from the statement what role Palo Alto, Calif.-based H-P's newly acquired Verifone unit would play in the alliance. Verifone is a leading supplier of electronic commerce systems. H-P closed the $1.29 billion acquisition of Verifone in late June.
An H-P spokesman was not immediately available to comment. The companies scheduled a conference call to discuss the deal at 1 p.m. EDT.
H-P's stock rose $2.25 to $63.44 in early afternoon trading, after reaching an all-time high of $63.625 on the New York Stock Exchange. AT&T was unchanged at $35.25, also on the NYSE.
